text:
Predicates:
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
ScheduleMeeting(x) ::: x schedules a meeting with their customers.
AppearCompany(x) ::: x will appear in the company today.
LunchCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
RemoteHome(x) ::: x is working remotely from home.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in other countries.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James.

Premises:
∀x ((Employee(x) ∧ ScheduleMeeting(x)) → AppearCompany(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchCompany(x) → ScheduleMeeting(x)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Employee(x) → (LunchCompany(x) ∨ LunchHome(x))) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
∀x (LunchHome(x) → RemoteHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x ((Employee(x) ∧ InOtherCountry(x)) → RemoteHome(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬RemoteHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(James) ∧ AppearCompany(James)) ⊕ ¬(Manager(James) ∨ AppearCompany(James)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.

Conclusion:
LunchCompany(James) ::: James has lunch in the company.
